title: Day 710 — Sheinbaum Holds Mañanera in Chiapas, Cites Security Gains and Reversal of Forced Displacement; Questions INE Straight-Ballot Criteria
detail: On September 11, 2026 (Day 710, Friday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas, alongside Governor Eduardo Ramírez Aguilar. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch reported that since December 2024 the state has recorded 9,949 detentions, 1,832 recovered vehicles, 1,545 seized weapons and 71,798 confiscated cartridges, plus 18.6 tonnes of drugs secured through 101,907 joint interinstitutional operations, alongside a 64% drop in the daily average of intentional homicides and a 44% drop in other high-impact crimes compared to December 2024; the governor cited incorporating 800 experienced officers and a 55% police salary increase. Officials said forced displacement in Chiapas — which shifted in character from religious conflicts toward territorial disputes among criminal groups — has substantially reversed, with roughly 95% of displaced families returned home, including in Comalapa and Chicomuselo municipalities where residents had fled into Guatemala. On literacy, Chiapas reported reaching 194,818 people since 2025 against a 250,000 target. Sheinbaum also asked the INE to clarify new criteria that would count unfolded "straight ballots" as valid votes, and argued the agency's 2027 election budget should be based on 2024 spending adjusted for inflation. Asked about PAN officials' trip to Europe during the early stage of the 2026–27 electoral process, she said, "Tienen derecho... pero tiene su simbolismo," noting the timing near Mexico's Independence Day.

media.caption: Sheinbaum holds her mañanera in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas, reporting security and displacement-reversal figures
